identity.name: Dawn
identity.description: Pakistan's leading English-language newspaper and digital outlet, covering national politics, security, business, culture and international affairs.

ownership.ownershipNotes: Flagship of Dawn Media Group, owned through Pakistan Herald Publications by the Haroon-Saigol family. It has a long record of editorial independence within Pakistan's constrained media environment.

editorialOrientation.evidence: Long-standing newspaper of record with a history of critical reporting on Pakistani governments and military influence, though commercial and political pressures persist.
editorialOrientation.source: Ownership and self-description via secondary references (official about page blocked or unavailable); secondary references; feed-level sample

politicalLeaning.evidence: No parsed MBFC rating; self-assessed as broadly centrist, liberal and institutional in tone.
politicalLeaning.source: Analyst assessment from publisher self-description, secondary references and feed-level sample

economicPerspective.evidence: Business coverage is substantial but not uniformly pro-market; editorials often emphasise state capacity and social development.
economicPerspective.source: Analyst assessment from business and economic coverage

internationalAlignment.evidence: National lens with strong attention to Pakistan's security, India relations and regional diplomacy.
internationalAlignment.source: Ownership, editorial positioning and regional coverage sample

reliability.evidence: Established newspaper of record with bylined reporting and corrections; no external factual rating parsed.
reliability.source: Analyst assessment from ownership, editorial record and feed-level sample

externalRatings.notes: No MBFC rating identified for Dawn.

intelligence.knownPerspective: Pakistani newspaper-of-record coverage. It frames events through national security, domestic politics and South Asian diplomacy, with a liberal editorial tradition.

selectionRationale: Adds essential Pakistani national coverage and a South Asian perspective absent from the current catalog.
